title: The Selector Sage
story: You have arrived at the ancient Library of Elements. The ancient tomes speak of powerful selectors — mystical incantations that allow you to locate any element in the DOM realm. Master the art of selection, and the library's secrets shall be yours.
objective: Use Playwright selectors to find the featured item by its ID, then verify its text content. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if the item's text is 'Magic Sword'.
hints: Use page.locator('#featured-item') to find an element by its ID.
Call .textContent() on the locator to retrieve the text inside the element.
Use an if-statement to compare the text, then console.log('LEVEL_PASSED') if it matches 'Magic Sword'.
explanation:
`page.locator(selector)` finds elements using CSS selectors, text, roles, or test IDs. It returns a Locator object — a lazy reference that only resolves when you call an action or assertion on it.

Common selector types:
• By ID: `page.locator('#featured-item')`
• By class: `page.locator('.item-rare')`
• By tag: `page.locator('h1')`
• By data attribute: `page.locator('[data-role="hero"]')`
• Chain to narrow: `page.locator('.list').locator('.item')`

Once you have a locator, call `.textContent()` to read its text:

```
const text = await page.locator('#featured-item').textContent();
if (text.trim() === 'Magic Sword') console.log('LEVEL_PASSED');
```

story: In the Hall of Truth, nothing is taken at face value. The great Asserters wield the power of expect() — they verify reality itself. Only by confirming what truly exists can you advance through this realm of verification.
objective: Use Playwright assertions to verify the page title says 'Hall of Truth' and the hero badge has class 'badge-gold'. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' after both assertions pass.

Use await expect(page.locator('#hero-badge')).toHaveClass(/badge-gold/) to assert a CSS class.
If both assertions pass (no errors thrown), log 'LEVEL_PASSED'. Wrap in try/catch if needed to debug.

title: The Waiter
story: The Realm of Async is treacherous. Elements appear and disappear like phantoms. Patience is not a weakness here — it is power. Master the art of waiting, and nothing in the dynamic web shall elude you.
objective: Wait for the delayed treasure chest to appear (it shows after 2 seconds), then read its data-treasure attribute. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if the value is 'golden-key'.
hints: Use await page.waitForSelector('#treasure-chest', { state: 'visible' }) to wait for the element to appear.
Alternatively, use await page.locator('#treasure-chest').waitFor({ state: 'visible' }).
After it's visible, use .getAttribute('data-treasure') to read the attribute, then compare and log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

story: The Marketplace of Many holds countless items, each with different properties. True masters can handle multiple elements at once — finding all, filtering the worthy, and verifying each in turn. Show your mastery of the many.
objective: Find all items in the marketplace list. Count how many have the class 'item-rare'. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if there are exactly 3 rare items.
hints: Use await page.locator('.marketplace-item').all() to get an array of all item locators.
Loop through the array and use locator.getAttribute('class') or locator.evaluate(el => el.classList.contains('item-rare')) to check each.
Count how many return true, then compare to 3 and log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Interceptor
story: In the Nexus of Networks, requests flow like rivers. The Interceptors are masters of traffic — they intercept API calls, redirect flows, and forge responses. Control the network, and you control the page's reality.
objective: Intercept the fake API call to '/api/items' and return a custom response with items containing a 'dragon-scale'. Then verify the page shows 'dragon-scale'. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Inside the route handler, call await route.fulfill({ contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ items: ['dragon-scale', 'fire-gem'] }) }).
After navigating, wait for the list to render: await page.waitForSelector('.item-entry').
Use page.getByText('dragon-scale').isVisible() to verify the intercepted response rendered correctly.

title: The Dialogue Keeper
story: The Oracle speaks through dialogs — alert, confirm, and prompt. Untrained testers freeze when these windows appear, blocking all progress. The Dialogue Keeper, however, intercepts them before they open. Listen for dialogs, respond wisely, and the Oracle's secrets are yours.
objective: Set up a dialog handler with page.on('dialog') to accept the confirm dialog, then click 'Challenge the Oracle'. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if #oracle-result contains 'Challenge Accepted!'.
hints: Register the listener BEFORE the action: page.on('dialog', async dialog => { await dialog.accept(); });
Then click: await page.click('#confirm-btn'). Playwright will auto-handle the dialog via your listener.
After clicking, wait a moment: await page.waitForTimeout(500), then read #oracle-result and check for 'Challenge Accepted!'.

story: Not all truths are visible in the DOM. Some secrets live only in the JavaScript realm — in window variables, computed values, and hidden state. The Evaluator steps beyond the boundary of HTML and reaches directly into the browser's soul with page.evaluate().

Use: const val = await page.evaluate(() => window.SECRET_RUNE);
Then simply: if (val === 'EXCALIBUR') console.log('LEVEL_PASSED');

title: The Shape Shifter
story: The web is a shapeshifter — it changes form depending on who is watching. Mobile devices see one world; desktops see another. The Shape Shifter can assume any form. Change your viewport, and previously invisible elements reveal themselves.
objective: Set the viewport to 375x667 (mobile), then check if #mobile-treasure is visible. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if it is.
hints: Use await page.setViewportSize({ width: 375, height: 667 }) to resize the viewport to iPhone size.
After resizing, the CSS media query (max-width: 480px) will trigger, showing the mobile-only element.
Check with: const visible = await page.locator('#mobile-treasure').isVisible(); then log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
explanation:
`page.setViewportSize({ width, height })` resizes the browser viewport. Use it to test responsive layouts.

```
await page.setViewportSize({ width: 375, height: 667 }); // iPhone SE
const treasure = page.locator('#mobile-treasure');
const visible = await treasure.isVisible();
if (visible) console.log('LEVEL_PASSED');
```

Common mobile sizes:
• iPhone SE: 375 × 667
• iPhone 12: 390 × 844
• iPad: 768 × 1024

Alternatively use `browser.newContext({ ...devices['iPhone 12'] })` to emulate a full device including user-agent.

Then check: const visible = await page.locator('#vault-content').isVisible(); and log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

objective: Add a cookie named 'vault-access' with value 'granted' for localhost, reload the page, then verify #vault-content is visible. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Use context.addCookies([{ name: 'vault-access', value: 'granted', url: 'http://host.docker.internal:4000' }]).
After adding the cookie, call await page.reload() so the page re-reads document.cookie.
Then check: const visible = await page.locator('#vault-content').isVisible(); and log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Uploader
story: The Scroll Repository demands an offering — a file, any file. The ancient custodian does not care about contents, only that the sacred act of upload is completed. Master setInputFiles(), and no upload gate shall stop you.
objective: Upload a file to #scroll-input using setInputFiles() with a Buffer (no real file needed). Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if #upload-success becomes visible.
hints: setInputFiles() accepts a virtual file object: { name, mimeType, buffer } — no actual file on disk needed.
Use: await page.locator('#scroll-input').setInputFiles({ name: 'spell.txt', mimeType: 'text/plain', buffer: Buffer.from('hello') });
Then wait: await page.locator('#upload-success').waitFor({ state: 'visible' }); and log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Tab Keeper
story: Some portals open doors to entirely new realms — new browser tabs that exist in parallel. The Tab Keeper does not lose track of these new pages. They listen for the popup event, step through the portal, and retrieve what lies beyond.
objective: Click #open-portal-btn, capture the new tab with page.waitForEvent('popup'), then get its title. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if the title is 'Secret Portal'.
hints: Use Promise.all to simultaneously wait for the popup and trigger the click — order matters here.
After getting the popup Page object: await popup.waitForLoadState(); to ensure it's fully loaded.
Then: const title = await popup.title(); if (title === 'Secret Portal') console.log('LEVEL_PASSED');

title: The Storage Sage
story: localStorage is a magical tome that persists across page loads — a silent memory that shapes how the page presents itself. The Storage Sage knows that identity can be rewritten between sessions. Set the right value, reload, and the page transforms completely.
objective: Use page.evaluate() to set localStorage item 'realm-rank' to 'archmage', then reload the page. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if #rank-display shows 'Grand Archmage'.
hints: Use await page.evaluate(() => localStorage.setItem('realm-rank', 'archmage')); to write to localStorage.
Then reload: await page.reload(); — the page re-reads localStorage on each load.
Read: const text = await page.locator('#rank-display').textContent(); then check if it includes 'Grand Archmage'.

title: The Sorcerer's Duel
story: The Shadow Sorcerer awaits. This boss challenge combines keyboard mastery with dialog handling. You must type the ancient incantation 'LUMINOS', then confirm your commitment when the sorcerer demands it. Hesitate and you lose. Act with precision and victory is yours.
objective: Type 'LUMINOS' into #spell-input using keyboard.type(), set up a dialog handler to accept the confirm, then trigger the duel. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if #duel-result has class 'victory'.
hints: Register the dialog handler before clicking the duel button: page.on('dialog', async d => await d.accept());
Type the spell first: await page.click('#spell-input'); await page.keyboard.type('LUMINOS');
Then click the duel button and check: const cls = await page.locator('#duel-result').getAttribute('class'); if (cls.includes('victory')) console.log('LEVEL_PASSED');

title: The Twin API Master
story: The dashboard draws from two springs: the Heroes Registry and the Quest Board. Both are real network requests — and both can be intercepted. The Twin API Master intercepts multiple routes in one test, mocking both feeds to show exactly what they want the page to display.
objective: Intercept both GET /api/heroes and GET /api/quests. Mock heroes with [{name:'Aria',class:'Mage',level:99}] and quests with [{title:'Slay the Dragon',difficulty:'Hard',reward:500}]. Then verify both items render on the page. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Route handlers must be set up BEFORE page.goto(). Both routes can be registered independently.
Use route.fulfill({ contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify({ heroes: [...] }) }) for each.
After navigation, check: await page.getByText('Aria').isVisible() and await page.getByText('Slay the Dragon').isVisible() — if both true, log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

objective: Add cookie 'nexus-pass'='open', click #open-nexus-btn to open the popup, wait for it, then verify #portal-access-msg contains 'Nexus Access Granted'. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Add the cookie to the context (not the page): await context.addCookies([{ name: 'nexus-pass', value: 'open', url: 'http://host.docker.internal:4000' }]);
Capture the popup with Promise.all — set up the waitForEvent before the click.
After await popup.waitForLoadState(), read: const text = await popup.locator('#portal-access-msg').textContent(); and check for 'Nexus Access Granted'.

title: The Rune Weaver
story: Three runes. Three slots. One hidden word. The Rune Weaver drags each rune to its destined position, then reads the result from both the DOM and localStorage — and immortalises the moment in a screenshot. Drag, evaluate, and chronicle.
objective: Drag all 3 runes to their correct slots (Sun→Slot I, Moon→Slot II, Star→Slot III). Then verify localStorage 'rune-word' equals 'PWY' via page.evaluate(). Take a screenshot and log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Do three separate dragAndDrop calls: #src-sun→#slot-1, #src-moon→#slot-2, #src-star→#slot-3.
After all drops, read storage: const word = await page.evaluate(() => localStorage.getItem('rune-word')); It should be 'PWY'.
Take a screenshot with await page.screenshot(), log its byte size, then if word === 'PWY' log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Archmage's Gauntlet
story: The final trial. Every skill you have mastered must now be wielded as one. Login the archmage. Open the settings panel. Mock the arcane feed API. Read the mana pool from the DOM via evaluate. Screenshot the dashboard. Only those who have truly learned the way of Playwright can claim this title.
objective: Login with 'archmage'/'shadowrealm', open the settings panel (#settings-btn), intercept /api/arcane-feed with custom spells, click 'Fetch Feed', read #mana-pool text via evaluate, take a screenshot. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Login: await page.fill('#username', 'archmage'); await page.fill('#password', 'shadowrealm'); await page.click('#login-btn'); await page.locator('#dashboard-section').waitFor({ state: 'visible' });
Open settings: await page.click('#settings-btn'); verify: await expect(page.locator('#settings-panel')).toBeVisible(); then close it.

Fetch the feed: await page.click('#fetch-api-btn'); await page.getByText('Arcane Blast').waitFor(); read mana: const mana = await page.evaluate(() => document.getElementById('mana-pool').textContent); take screenshot: await page.screenshot({ fullPage: true }); then log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
explanation:
This is the most complex level — it chains login, navigation, route mocking, and `page.evaluate()`.

Steps:
1. Set up `/api/arcane-feed` route mock before `goto()`
2. Fill credentials and click login
3. Click settings, close it
4. Click "Fetch Feed" to trigger the mocked route
5. Read `#mana-pool` text via `page.evaluate()`

`page.evaluate(fn)` runs JavaScript in the browser context and returns the result:
```
const manaPool = await page.evaluate(
  () => document.getElementById('mana-pool').textContent
);
```

title: The Double Clicker
story: In the Archive of Arcane Files, a tome hides its secrets behind a double-click. A single click merely selects — you must strike twice in swift succession to unlock the rename ritual. Master the art of the double-click and rename the ancient tome.
objective: Double-click on the file '#target-file' (tome.md) to open the rename box. Then type a new name in '#rename-input' and press Enter. Verify '#rename-success' is visible. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Use await page.dblclick('#target-file') — this fires both a click AND a dblclick event, which opens the rename box.
After double-clicking, the #rename-input should appear. Use await page.fill('#rename-input', 'new-name.md') to set the new value.
Press Enter with await page.keyboard.press('Enter') to confirm. Then check await page.locator('#rename-success').isVisible() and log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Filter Sage
story: The Guild Roster is crowded. Seven adventurers of varying status and class have registered. The Sage needs only Active Mages — those rare few who wield the arcane arts and stand ready for battle. Learn to chain locator filters to find the worthy among the many.
objective: Find all active mage guild members by chaining locator.filter() calls. First filter '.guild-member' for those with '.member-status.Active', then filter again for those containing 'Mage'. Count them and log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if there are exactly 2.
hints: Use page.locator('.guild-member') to get all 7 members, then chain .filter({ has: page.locator('.member-status.Active') }) to keep only active ones.
Chain a second .filter({ hasText: 'Mage' }) to keep only those whose text contains 'Mage' (matches both 'Mage · Fire School' and 'Mage · Shadow School').
Use await activeMages.count() to get the number. There should be exactly 2 active mages. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if count === 2.

title: The Response Watcher
story: The Oracle speaks only through the network. When the button is pressed, a hidden request is sent to the oracle's data scroll. A true Watcher intercepts this response and reads the prophecy within — verifying the oracle's confidence before trusting her words.
objective: Click '#consult-btn' to trigger a fetch to oracle-data.json. Use page.waitForResponse() to capture the response. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if the response status is 200.
hints: The key: set up the waitForResponse promise BEFORE clicking the button. Use: const responsePromise = page.waitForResponse(resp => resp.url().includes('oracle-data.json'));
Then click: await page.click('#consult-btn'); then resolve the promise: const response = await responsePromise;
Parse the response: const data = await response.json(); then check data.confidence === 99 and log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Network Blocker
story: The Cursed Vault loads two malevolent scrolls that taint everything they touch. Before even entering the vault, a skilled Blocker must intercept these cursed requests and abort them. Only when the vault detects both requests aborted will it enter protection mode.

After goto(), wait for the async fetch handlers: await page.waitForSelector('#protection-msg', { state: 'visible', timeout: 5000 }); then check isVisible() and log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Dark Mage
story: The Shadow Realm is only accessible to those who embrace the darkness. The page reads the system color scheme preference and reveals hidden knowledge only to those who walk in dark mode. A true Dark Mage must instruct the browser to appear as a dark-mode devotee.

hints: Call await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' }) before page.goto(). This makes the page's matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') return true.
The page reads the media query on load and sets the realm indicator text accordingly.
After navigating, read the text: const text = await page.locator('#realm-indicator').textContent(); If text === 'Shadow Realm', log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Time Bender
story: The Ancient One sleeps behind a 30-second seal. In the real world, you would wait. But a Time Bender bends the clock itself — installing a fake timer and fast-forwarding 30 seconds in an instant. Time is not a constraint; it is a tool.
objective: Install the fake clock with page.clock.install() BEFORE navigating. Navigate to the page. Run the clock forward 31 seconds. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if #awakened-msg is visible.
hints: Call await page.clock.install() BEFORE page.goto(). This replaces the browser's real timers with Playwright-controlled fake ones.
After navigating, call await page.clock.runFor(30000) to advance time by 30,000ms — this fires ALL setInterval callbacks in chronological order (unlike fastForward which only fires each timer once).
Then check: const visible = await page.locator('#awakened-msg').isVisible(); if (visible) console.log('LEVEL_PASSED');

title: The Style Inspector
story: Beyond text and visibility lies a deeper truth — the visual properties of elements. The Arcane Gallery holds a legendary hero card. Its data-rarity attribute, its golden border, its power bar role — all must be verified with precision. Inspect everything.
objective: Use @playwright/test's expect with toHaveAttribute, toHaveCSS, and toHaveRole. Verify: #hero-card has data-rarity='legendary'; #hero-card has CSS border-style='solid'; #power-bar has ARIA role 'progressbar'. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' after all assertions pass.
hints: Import expect from @playwright/test: const { expect } = require('@playwright/test'); This gives you access to toHaveAttribute, toHaveCSS, and toHaveRole.
Check the attribute: await expect(page.locator('#hero-card')).toHaveAttribute('data-rarity', 'legendary'); and CSS: await expect(page.locator('#hero-card')).toHaveCSS('border-style', 'solid');
For the ARIA role: await expect(page.locator('#power-bar')).toHaveRole('progressbar'); The role='progressbar' is set explicitly on the element. If all pass without throwing, log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Location Oracle
story: The Oracle reads the coordinates of those who seek her wisdom, but she demands permission first. You must create a browser context that grants geolocation access and sets a precise location. Only then will the oracle reveal the ancient coordinates of London.
objective: Create a browser context with grantPermissions(['geolocation']) and setGeolocation({ latitude: 51.5074, longitude: -0.1278 }). Create a page from that context. Navigate, click '#locate-btn', wait for '#location-display' to appear, verify '#lat-display' contains '51'. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Permissions must be set on a CONTEXT, not a page. Create a context: const context = await browser.newContext(); then await context.grantPermissions(['geolocation']);
Set the location: await context.setGeolocation({ latitude: 51.5074, longitude: -0.1278 }); Then create a page from the context: const page = await context.newPage();

After goto(), click '#locate-btn', wait: await page.locator('#location-display').waitFor({ state: 'visible' }); read lat: const lat = await page.locator('#lat-display').textContent(); if (lat.includes('51')) log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

objective: Create a browser context with grantPermissions(['geolocation']) and setGeolocation({ latitude: 51.5074, longitude: -0.1278 }). Create a page from that context. Navigate, click '#locate-btn', wait for '#location-display' to appear, verify '#lat-display' contains '51'. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Permissions must be set on a CONTEXT, not a page. Create a context: const context = await browser.newContext(); then await context.grantPermissions(['geolocation']);
Set the location: await context.setGeolocation({ latitude: 51.5074, longitude: -0.1278 }); Then create a page from the context: const page = await context.newPage();

After goto(), click '#locate-btn', wait: await page.locator('#location-display').waitFor({ state: 'visible' }); read lat: const lat = await page.locator('#lat-display').textContent(); if (lat.includes('51')) log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Resilient Tester
story: The final trial of the ultimate Playwright master. The Mana Wellspring fills gradually over time — no events, no promises, just slow accumulation. A Resilient Tester does not wait blindly nor poll naively. They wield expect.poll() to retry assertions until the stars align and the mana reaches its peak.
objective: The wellspring's #mana-bar fills via data-level attribute (0 to 100) over ~2 seconds. Use expect.poll() to wait until data-level equals '100'. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' when ready.
hints: expect.poll() repeatedly calls an async function until the result satisfies the assertion. Import expect from @playwright/test first.
Use: await expect.poll(async () => { const v = await page.locator('#mana-bar').getAttribute('data-level'); return parseInt(v); }, { timeout: 15000 }).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(100);
After polling succeeds, check: const ready = await page.locator('#ready-msg').isVisible(); if (ready) console.log('LEVEL_PASSED');

title: The Hoverer
story: The Hover Sanctum guards its spells behind invisible barriers. A simple click reveals nothing — only by hovering over the menu does the dropdown appear, and only then can the spell be selected. Master the hover, and the sanctum's powers are yours.
objective: Hover over '#menu-spells' to reveal the dropdown. Then click '#spell-lightning' to select Lightning Bolt. Verify '#selected-spell' contains 'Lightning Bolt'. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Use await page.locator('#menu-spells').hover() to simulate hovering — this triggers the CSS :hover state that reveals the dropdown.
After hovering, the dropdown is visible and #spell-lightning becomes clickable. Use await page.locator('#spell-lightning').click();
Read the result: const text = await page.locator('#selected-spell').textContent(); if (text.includes('Lightning Bolt')) console.log('LEVEL_PASSED');

title: The Index Master
story: The Champions Board lists warriors by rank. You cannot know their names in advance — you must navigate by position. The first is the champion, the last the challenger, and the third holds a special secret. Index-based selection is the key.
objective: Use locator.first() to get rank 1's name, locator.last() to get rank 5's name, and locator.nth(2) to get rank 3's name. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if all three are non-empty strings.
hints: Use page.locator('.rank-entry').first() to get the first element, then chain .locator('.champion-name').textContent() to read the name.
Use .last() for the 5th entry. Use .nth(2) for the 3rd entry (nth is 0-indexed, so nth(0)=1st, nth(2)=3rd).
Rank 1 should be 'Varek Shadowcall', rank 5 is 'Celith Dawnblade'. Check both, then log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Count Keeper
story: The Rarity Vault holds seven items of varying power. Most are common or rare — but only three are legendary. A Count Keeper does not manually count; they assert the exact number using toHaveCount. Filter, then verify.
objective: Click '#filter-legendary' to show only legendary items. Then use expect(locator).toHaveCount(3) to verify exactly 3 are visible. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: First click the filter: await page.click('#filter-legendary'); This hides non-legendary items by adding class 'hidden'.
Use: await expect(page.locator('.item-card:not(.hidden)')).toHaveCount(3); This selects all non-hidden item cards and asserts exactly 3.
toHaveCount() throws if the count doesn't match. If it passes without error, then log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Value Inspector
story: The Binding Ritual form holds state — pre-filled values, checked oaths, and a locked submit button. An Inspector does not just look; they assert. Verify each field's state with precision before the seal is complete.
objective: Verify: '#guild-name' has value 'Order of the Arcane' (toHaveValue), '#oath-truth' is checked (toBeChecked), '#submit-btn' is disabled initially (toBeDisabled). Fill '#mage-title', then verify '#submit-btn' is enabled (toBeEnabled). Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Use await expect(page.locator('#guild-name')).toHaveValue('Order of the Arcane'); for input value assertion.
For checkbox: await expect(page.locator('#oath-truth')).toBeChecked(); For disabled: await expect(page.locator('#submit-btn')).toBeDisabled();
After await page.fill('#mage-title', 'Grand Sorcerer');, the button enables. Assert: await expect(page.locator('#submit-btn')).toBeEnabled(); then log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The URL Oracle
story: The Waypoint Nexus teleports between realms by changing the URL. A URL Oracle does not just navigate — they assert the exact destination. Use waitForURL to confirm arrival, then seal the truth with toHaveURL.
objective: Navigate to the page. Click '#wp-void' to travel to the Void Realm. Use page.waitForURL('**/#void-realm') to wait for the URL change. Then assert with expect(page).toHaveURL(/#void-realm/). Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: After clicking '#wp-void', the page uses window.location.hash = 'void-realm' which changes the URL to .../level-40/#void-realm.
Use await page.waitForURL('**/#void-realm') to wait for this URL change to complete.
Then assert: await expect(page).toHaveURL(/#void-realm/); — the regex matches any URL containing 'void-realm'. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if all assertions pass.

title: The Request Modifier
story: The Spell Catalogue fetches its data from the arcane network. A Request Modifier does not merely intercept — they fetch the real response, alter its contents, and send back a modified version. The first spell's power must be raised to 9999.
objective: Use page.route() with route.fetch() to intercept '**/spell-catalogue.json'. Fetch the real response, add 'power: 9000' to the first spell, and fulfill with modified JSON. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if spell cards appear.
hints: Inside the route handler: const response = await route.fetch(); fetches the real data from the server.
const data = await response.json(); gives you the parsed JSON. Modify: data.spells[0].power = 9999; then await route.fulfill({ json: data });
After clicking #fetch-btn and waiting for .spell-card, check: const power = await page.locator('.spell-power').first().getAttribute('data-power'); if (power === '9999') log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Mouse Wizard
story: The Mana Conduit is a custom slider that rejects all fill() attempts. It was crafted by an ancient wizard who trusted only raw mouse control. To charge it, you must move the mouse to its track, press the mouse button, drag to the end, and release. Only then will it be fully charged.
objective: Get #slider-track's bounding box. Use page.mouse.move, mouse.down, and mouse.up to drag the slider to the far right. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if #mana-value shows '100%'.
hints: Get the bounding box first: const box = await page.locator('#slider-track').boundingBox(); This gives you { x, y, width, height }.
Simulate the drag: await page.mouse.move(box.x, box.y + box.height/2); await page.mouse.down(); await page.mouse.move(box.x + box.width, box.y + box.height/2, { steps: 20 }); await page.mouse.up();
The { steps: 20 } option fires 20 intermediate mousemove events for smooth dragging. Check: const val = await page.locator('#mana-value').textContent(); if (val === '100%') log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Load Watcher
story: The Summoning Circle brings entities from the void one by one — each through a separate network request. A hasty tester asserts before all entities arrive and finds only partial results. A Load Watcher waits for the network to fall silent before making any claims.
objective: Click '#summon-btn' to start the ritual. Use page.waitForLoadState('networkidle') to wait for all async fetches to complete. Then assert all 4 entity cards appeared using toHaveCount(4). Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Click the button: await page.click('#summon-btn'); This starts 4 sequential async fetches with delays up to 2 seconds.
Wait for network silence: await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle'); This waits until no network requests have occurred for 500ms.
Then assert: await expect(page.locator('.entity-card.appeared')).toHaveCount(4); If all 4 arrived, log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

title: The Mobile Shapeshifter
story: The Shapeshifter's page wears different forms for different visitors. Desktop users see a full navigation bar. Mobile users see a hamburger menu and a special mobile banner. A true Shapeshifter Tester can become any device — and assert what that device would see.
objective: Use const { devices } = require('playwright') and create a context with browser.newContext({ ...devices['iPhone 12'] }). Navigate to the page. Verify '#hamburger' is visible and '#layout-badge' contains 'Mobile Experience'. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Import devices: const { chromium, devices } = require('playwright'); then const iPhone = devices['iPhone 12']; const context = await browser.newContext({ ...iPhone });
Spread the device config: { ...iPhone } sets the userAgent, viewport (390x844), and touch capabilities for iPhone 12.

After navigating, check: const visible = await page.locator('#hamburger').isVisible(); const text = await page.locator('#layout-badge').textContent(); if (visible && text.includes('Mobile Experience')) log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

hints: Use locator.check() to check a checkbox — it only checks if not already checked. Use locator.uncheck() to reverse it.

locator.inputValue() returns the current value of an input or select element as a string. Compare it to verify the selection.

title: The State Warden
story: The Locked Vault guards its secrets behind disabled gates, hidden runes, and sealed inscriptions. Not every truth needs an assertion — some elements reveal their state through direct boolean queries.
objective: Check isEnabled() on #locked-gate (should be false), isHidden() on #secret-rune (should be true), isEditable() on #sealed-input (should be false). If all three match, log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: locator.isEnabled() returns true if the element is not disabled. A button with the disabled attribute returns false.
locator.isHidden() returns true if the element has display:none, visibility:hidden, or is otherwise invisible.
locator.isEditable() returns true if the element is an input/textarea that is not readonly and not disabled. A readonly input returns false.
explanation:
State inspection methods return booleans directly (no assertion needed):

• `isEnabled()` → true if element has no `disabled` attribute
• `isDisabled()` → true if element has `disabled` attribute
• `isVisible()` → true if element is in the DOM and not hidden
• `isHidden()` → true if element is hidden or not in DOM
• `isEditable()` → true if element is not `readonly` and not `disabled`

```
const gateEnabled = await page.locator('#locked-gate').isEnabled();    // false
const runeHidden  = await page.locator('#secret-rune').isHidden();     // true
const inputEdit   = await page.locator('#sealed-input').isEditable();  // false
if (!gateEnabled && runeHidden && !inputEdit) console.log('LEVEL_PASSED');
```

title: The Locator Alchemist
story: In the Spell Matrix, elements overlap and multiply. A button may be many things at once. The Locator Alchemist combines two queries into one unstoppable force with .and(), and casts a wide net with .or().
objective: Use page.getByRole('button').and(page.getByText('Fire Strike')) to find the Fire Strike button and verify its text. Use page.locator('.spell').or(page.locator('.rune')) to find all 6 combined items. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: locator.and(otherLocator) narrows down results — the element must match BOTH locators. Like an intersection.
locator.or(otherLocator) broadens results — the element must match EITHER locator. Like a union.
Count with await allItems.count() — there are 3 .spell and 3 .rune elements, totalling 6.

title: The Locator Alchemist — locator.and narrows to intersection
story: In the Spell Matrix, elements overlap and multiply. A button may be many things at once. The Locator Alchemist combines two queries into one unstoppable force with .and(), and casts a wide net with .or().
objective: Use page.getByRole('button').and(page.getByText('Fire Strike')) to find the Fire Strike button and verify its text. Use page.locator('.spell').or(page.locator('.rune')) to find all 6 combined items. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: locator.and(otherLocator) narrows down results — the element must match BOTH locators. Like an intersection.
locator.or(otherLocator) broadens results — the element must match EITHER locator. Like a union.
Count with await allItems.count() — there are 3 .spell and 3 .rune elements, totalling 6.

title: The Focus Keeper
story: The Arcane Portal Form can only be navigated by a true keyboard warrior. No mouse shall touch these fields. Focus must be given, then passed through Tab — and only the one who knows where focus lands shall unlock the portal.
objective: Focus #realm-input with locator.focus(). Press Tab twice with page.keyboard.press('Tab'). Evaluate document.activeElement.id. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED' if the active element is 'power-input'.
hints: locator.focus() programmatically focuses an element — equivalent to clicking it without triggering a click event.
page.keyboard.press('Tab') moves focus to the next focusable element in DOM order.
page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement.id) returns the id of the currently focused element. Two Tabs from #realm-input lands on #power-input.

title: The Condition Oracle
story: The Mana Crystal charges itself over time, ticking upward every 600ms. You cannot wait for a selector — there is no selector to wait for. Only a custom condition, born from your own predicate, can know when the mana is ready.
objective: Use page.waitForFunction(() => parseInt(document.getElementById('mana-counter').textContent) >= 5). After it resolves, read the counter value. If it is 5 or more, log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: page.waitForFunction(fn) polls the provided function in the browser context until it returns a truthy value.
The function runs in the browser — use standard DOM APIs like document.getElementById() inside it.
After waitForFunction resolves, the condition is guaranteed to have been true. Read the counter with locator.textContent() and parse it with parseInt().

title: The API Summoner
story: The true API warrior needs no browser — no viewport, no DOM, no clicks. Armed only with Playwright's APIRequestContext, they speak directly to the server in the language of HTTP: GET, POST, JSON.
objective: Use chromium.request.newContext() to create an API context. GET /pages/level-57/grimoire.json. Verify the response status is 200 and the body is JSON. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Use playwright.request.newContext() (not chromium.request) to create a standalone HTTP client — no browser required. Set baseURL to avoid repeating the host.
await request.get(path) makes an HTTP GET. The response object has .ok() (boolean), .status() (number), .json() (parsed body), .text() (raw string).
await response.json() parses the response body as JSON. Check body.spellCount === 5, then dispose: await request.dispose().

title: The Trace Keeper
story: The Arcane Observatory captures every spell, every click, every network whisper. Playwright's trace recorder writes a full chronicle of the test — screenshots, DOM snapshots, and network logs in a single archive.
objective: Start tracing with context.tracing.start({ screenshots: true, snapshots: true }). Navigate to the page and click the button. Stop tracing with context.tracing.stop({ path: '/tmp/trace-58.zip' }). Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Call context.tracing.start() BEFORE creating pages or navigating — it must be active to capture early events.
{ screenshots: true, snapshots: true } captures visual screenshots and DOM snapshots at each action step.
context.tracing.stop({ path }) writes the trace zip file. Open it at trace.playwright.dev to replay your test.

title: The HAR Recorder
story: The Network Nexus hums with requests and responses. An HAR archive captures the full conversation — every URL, status code, header, and body — for later inspection, replay, or mocking.
objective: Create a context with recordHar: { path: '/tmp/network-59.har' }. Navigate to the level page (it makes fetch requests on load). Close the context to flush the HAR. Log 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
hints: Pass recordHar: { path: '...' } when creating the browser context — HAR recording starts immediately for all pages in that context.
The HAR file is only written when the context is closed (await context.close()). Closing the browser without closing the context first may not flush it.
The HAR file is a JSON archive you can open in browser DevTools (Network tab → Import HAR) to replay and inspect all recorded requests.

title: The Download Warden
story: Files fall from the sky. The Download Warden intercepts them using page.waitForEvent('download') — catching every file before it lands.
objective: Use page.waitForEvent('download') to intercept a file download.
hints: Use Promise.all([page.waitForEvent('download'), triggerAction()]) to avoid race conditions
download.suggestedFilename() returns the file name
download.path() returns the temporary file path after download completes

title: The Download Warden — saves file to disk
story: Once caught, the Warden saves the download to a specific path using download.saveAs().
objective: Save a downloaded file to disk using download.saveAs().
hints: download.saveAs(path) copies the file to the specified path
Use a /tmp/ path for temporary test files
The file is ready to read after saveAs() resolves

title: The Download Warden — reads download path
story: The Warden inspects the temporary path where the file was stored by the browser.
objective: Use download.path() to get the temporary file path.
hints: download.path() returns null if the download failed
The temporary path is managed by Playwright — use saveAs() to persist it
download.path() is async and returns a Promise

title: The Download Warden — reads suggested filename
story: The Warden reads the suggested filename from the download header before saving.
objective: Use download.suggestedFilename() to get the original file name.
hints: download.suggestedFilename() returns the filename from Content-Disposition or the URL
This is synchronous — no await needed
Use it to validate the file name before saving

title: The Download Warden — cancels a download
story: Not all files are welcome. The Warden cancels unwanted downloads using download.cancel().
objective: Cancel a download in progress using download.cancel().
hints: download.cancel() cancels the download and rejects the path promise
After cancelling, download.path() returns null
Useful for testing UI behaviour when a download is aborted

title: The WebSocket Watcher
story: Real-time connections flow through WebSockets. The Watcher listens on page.on('websocket') to observe every connection the page opens.
objective: Use page.on('websocket') to intercept a WebSocket connection.
hints: page.on('websocket', ws => { }) fires for every WebSocket created
ws.url() returns the WebSocket endpoint URL
ws.on('framesent', data => { }) and ws.on('framereceived', data => { }) monitor messages

title: The WebSocket Watcher — monitors sent frames
story: Every message sent through the socket is a frame. The Watcher tracks outgoing frames with ws.on('framesent').
objective: Listen to framesent events on a WebSocket connection.
hints: ws.on('framesent', frame => { frame.payload }) gives you the sent message
frame.payload is a string or Buffer
Set up the listener before the WebSocket is used to avoid missing messages

title: The WebSocket Watcher — monitors received frames
story: Incoming messages tell the story of the server response. The Watcher captures them with ws.on('framereceived').
objective: Listen to framereceived events on a WebSocket.
hints: ws.on('framereceived', frame => { }) fires for each incoming message
frame.payload is the message content
Combine with framesent to build a full message log

title: The WebSocket Watcher — detects WebSocket URL
story: The Watcher reads the WebSocket endpoint URL to verify the app is connecting to the right server.
objective: Read the URL of an intercepted WebSocket connection.
hints: ws.url() returns the full WebSocket URL
Use this to verify the correct endpoint is being used
Combine with an assertion to fail the test if the URL is wrong

title: The WebSocket Watcher — detects WebSocket close
story: Every connection eventually closes. The Watcher detects it with ws.on('close').
objective: Listen for the WebSocket close event.
hints: ws.on('close', () => { }) fires when the socket closes
The close event fires for both normal and abnormal closures
Useful for detecting unexpected disconnections in tests

title: The Bridge Builder
story: The Bridge Builder connects the Node.js world to the browser with page.exposeFunction() — making server-side functions callable from page scripts.
objective: Use page.exposeFunction() to expose a Node.js function to the browser.
hints: page.exposeFunction('name', fn) adds fn to window.name in the browser
The function can be async and returns a Promise in the browser
Call it from page.evaluate() or page scripts

title: The Bridge Builder — async exposed function
story: The bridge carries async cargo too. An exposed function can return a Promise, and the browser awaits it.
objective: Expose an async function and await its result in the browser.
hints: Async functions exposed via exposeFunction return Promises in the browser
Use await window.myFunc() in evaluate
This lets you call fs.readFile or database queries from the browser context

title: The Bridge Builder — exposes binding with handle
story: page.exposeBinding() is the advanced bridge — it receives a source object with the page and frame context alongside the arguments.
objective: Use page.exposeBinding() to expose a function that receives context info.
hints: page.exposeBinding('name', (source, ...args) => { source.page }) gives you the page reference
source.frame is the calling frame, source.page is the page
Use { handle: true } option to get JSHandle arguments instead of plain values

title: The Bridge Builder — exposes function on context
story: The bridge can span all pages in a context. context.exposeFunction() makes the function available in every new page.
objective: Use context.exposeFunction() to expose a function across all pages.
hints: context.exposeFunction() works just like page.exposeFunction() but for all pages
Must be called before creating pages (or they won't have the function)
Useful for shared utilities like logging or ID generation

title: The Bridge Builder — reads file from browser context
story: The Bridge Builder's ultimate trick: reading a file from Node.js via a browser-triggered call.
objective: Use page.exposeFunction() to read a Node.js file from within page.evaluate().
hints: Expose fs.readFileSync wrapped in an async function
Call it from evaluate to get file contents in the browser context
This pattern lets tests read config files from within browser scripts

title: The Spell Inscriber
story: Some magic must be cast before the page awakens. The Spell Inscriber uses page.addInitScript() to inject code that runs before any page scripts load.
objective: Use page.addInitScript() to inject a script that runs before page load.
hints: page.addInitScript(fn) runs fn in the browser before the page scripts execute
The function runs in the browser context — no Node.js access
Use it to mock globals, override APIs, or set up test state before load

title: The Spell Inscriber — passes args to init script
story: The Inscriber carries data into the scroll. page.addInitScript() accepts a { content } string or a function with an arg parameter.
objective: Pass a value into page.addInitScript() via script content.
hints: page.addInitScript({ content: `window.X = ${value}` }) lets you template values in
For object args use JSON.stringify()
This runs before the page loads so the values are ready for the app immediately

title: The Spell Inscriber — mocks a browser API
story: The Inscriber replaces built-in browser APIs before the page can use them — mocking Date.now() or Math.random() for deterministic tests.
objective: Use page.addInitScript() to override a built-in browser API.
hints: Override Date by setting window.Date in the init script
Math.random can be replaced with () => 0.5 for deterministic tests
This is more reliable than hooking after load because app code runs after the init script

title: The Spell Inscriber — applies to all pages via context
story: The Inscriber can brand all pages in a context. context.addInitScript() applies to every page opened in that context.
objective: Use context.addInitScript() so the script runs in every page of the context.
hints: context.addInitScript() must be called before opening pages

title: The Spell Inscriber — injects a script from file

objective: Use page.addInitScript() with a file path to inject a script.

title: The HTML Archivist
story: The HTML Archivist captures the entire DOM as a string using page.content() — useful for snapshot testing, scraping, and debugging.
objective: Use page.content() to get the full HTML of the page.
hints: page.content() returns the full serialised HTML as a string
It includes the <html>, <head> and <body> tags
Useful for comparing page state before and after an action

title: The HTML Archivist — checks for specific element in HTML

objective: Check that page.content() contains a specific HTML element.
hints: page.content() returns a string — use .includes() to search it

title: The HTML Archivist — compares content before and after

objective: Capture page.content() before and after an action and compare the results.
hints: Call page.content() before the action, then again after
Compare the two strings to verify something changed
This is useful for smoke-testing dynamic content

title: The HTML Archivist — measures content length
story: The length of the HTML indicates the richness of the page. The Archivist measures it to detect empty pages.
objective: Assert that page.content() returns a string with meaningful length.
hints: A blank page has very short HTML — typically < 200 chars
Real pages are usually > 500 chars
page.content().length gives the byte size of the serialized DOM

title: The HTML Archivist — uses innerHTML for a specific element

objective: Use locator.innerHTML() to get the inner HTML of a specific element.
hints: locator.innerHTML() returns the inner HTML as a string
Different from textContent() — it includes child tags
Use it to verify dynamic template rendering

title: The PDF Scribe
story: The PDF Scribe freezes pages into permanent documents using page.pdf() — generating reports and invoices for testing.
objective: Use page.pdf() to generate a PDF buffer from the current page.
hints: page.pdf() only works in headless Chromium — not Firefox or WebKit
It returns a Buffer containing the PDF data
Pass { path } to save directly to disk

title: The PDF Scribe — saves PDF to disk
story: The Scribe writes the PDF to a file using the path option so it persists after the test.
objective: Use page.pdf({ path }) to save the PDF directly to a file.
hints: page.pdf({ path: '/tmp/page.pdf' }) saves to disk
When path is provided, the method still returns the Buffer
Verify the file exists with fs.existsSync()

title: The PDF Scribe — sets page format

page.pdf({ format: 'A4' }) generates A4-sized PDF

title: The PDF Scribe — prints background graphics

hints: printBackground: true enables CSS background colors and images in the PDF

Default is false — backgrounds are stripped

title: The PDF Scribe — sets margin

Margins affect page breaks and content overflow

title: The Offline Oracle
story: The Offline Oracle severs the network connection using context.setOffline(true) — testing how the app behaves when the internet disappears.
objective: Use context.setOffline(true) to simulate a network outage.
hints: context.setOffline(true) makes all network requests fail immediately
context.setOffline(false) restores connectivity
Test offline UI states like "No connection" banners

title: The Offline Oracle — restores connectivity
story: After the outage, the Oracle restores the connection and verifies the app recovers.
objective: Toggle offline mode off using context.setOffline(false) and verify the page loads.
hints: Set offline, then set back to false, then try navigating
Test the reload or retry logic in your app
context.setOffline() affects all pages in the context

title: The Offline Oracle — checks offline error type
story: When offline, navigation throws a specific error. The Oracle catches and identifies it.
objective: Catch the navigation error thrown when context.setOffline(true) is active.
hints: The error message typically contains "net::ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED" or similar
Wrap the goto in try/catch to handle it gracefully
Use error.message to inspect what kind of failure occurred

title: The Offline Oracle — tests cached content
story: The Oracle loads a page first, then goes offline to check if cached content still renders.
objective: Load a page while online, go offline, then reload to test cache behaviour.
hints: Service workers and browser cache may serve content when offline
After going offline, page.reload() may still show content from cache
Test the difference between cached and uncached offline states

title: The Offline Oracle — blocks specific resources
story: More surgical than full offline mode — the Oracle blocks specific domains using page.route() while letting others through.
objective: Use page.route() to block requests to a specific origin instead of using setOffline.
hints: page.route('**/api/**', route => route.abort()) blocks all API calls
This is more targeted than context.setOffline() which blocks everything
Combine with route.fulfill() to return a "network error" response

title: The State Inspector
story: The State Inspector checks whether elements are hidden, disabled, or editable — without making assertions that fail tests.
objective: Use locator.isHidden() to check if an element is not visible.
hints: locator.isHidden() returns true if the element is hidden or not in the DOM
isHidden() is the opposite of isVisible()
Both return a boolean — use them in if-else for conditional logic
explanation:
`isHidden()` and `isVisible()` check CSS visibility, `display: none`, and presence in the DOM.

```
const hidden = await page.locator('body').isHidden();   // false (body is always visible)
const visible = await page.locator('body').isVisible(); // true
```

For a hidden element (`display:none` or `visibility:hidden`):
• `isHidden()` → `true`
• `isVisible()` → `false`
• `isEnabled()` → still depends on the `disabled` attribute

title: The State Inspector — isDisabled check

objective: Use locator.isDisabled() to check if a form element is disabled.

title: The Text Harvester
story: The Text Harvester gathers text from every matching element at once using locator.allTextContents() — no loops needed.

```
const texts = await page.locator('h2').allTextContents();

title: The Selector Sage
story: You have arrived at the ancient Library of Elements. The ancient tomes speak of powerful selectors — mystical incantations that allow you to locate any element in the DOM realm. Master Cypress's art of selection, and the library's secrets shall be yours.
objective: Use cy.get() to find the featured item by its ID and assert its text equals 'Magic Sword'.
hints: Use cy.get('#featured-item') to select the target element, then chain .should() to assert its state.
.should('have.text', 'Magic Sword') retries automatically until it passes or times out.
Cypress marks the test as passed when all assertions succeed — no console.log needed.
explanation:
`cy.get(selector)` finds elements using CSS selectors — the core Cypress command for selecting DOM elements.

```
cy.get('#featured-item')                   // by ID
cy.get('.item-rare')                       // by class
cy.get('[data-role="hero"]')              // by attribute
cy.get('.list').find('.item')              // chain to narrow down
```

`cy.get()` automatically retries until the element exists (default 4 s timeout). All subsequent commands chain off the yielded element.

title: The Shape Shifter
story: The web shapeshifts depending on who is watching. Cypress's cy.viewport() changes the browser size instantly, revealing elements that are only visible on mobile screens.
objective: Set the viewport to 375x667 (mobile), then assert '#mobile-treasure' is visible.
hints: Start with: cy.viewport(375, 667)
Then: cy.get('#mobile-treasure').should('be.visible')
Cypress marks the test as passed when all assertions succeed — no console.log needed.
explanation:
`cy.viewport(width, height)` resizes the viewport for responsive testing.

```
cy.viewport(375, 667);   // iPhone SE
cy.get('#mobile-treasure').should('be.visible');
```

Or use device presets: `cy.viewport('iphone-6')`, `cy.viewport('macbook-13')`

`expect(value).toEqual(expected)` does a **deep equality** check — it compares object/array contents recursively, unlike `toBe` which uses `===`.

```
expect({ a: 1, b: [2, 3] }).toEqual({ a: 1, b: [2, 3] }); // passes
expect({ a: 1 }).toBe({ a: 1 });                           // FAILS (different object refs)
```

objective: Use toHaveBeenNthCalledWith to assert the arguments of a specific call.
hints: toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(n, ...args) — checks the nth call (1-indexed).
2nd call: toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(2, ...).
Useful when testing that different calls had different arguments.
solution:
const deliver=jest.fn();deliver('scroll of fire');deliver('scroll of ice');deliver('scroll of lightning');
test('second delivery was ice',()=>{expect(deliver).toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(2,'scroll of ice');});

title: toHaveReturned
story: The function must complete without throwing and actually return something.
objective: Use toHaveReturned and toHaveReturnedWith to assert return values.
hints: toHaveReturned() — passes if the mock returned at least once (did not throw).
toHaveReturnedWith(value) — checks if any call returned that value.
toHaveLastReturnedWith(value) — checks the last return value.

title: jest.spyOn Basics
story: Spy on the blacksmith's hammer method without replacing it.
objective: Use jest.spyOn to spy on an existing method while keeping its implementation.
hints: jest.spyOn(obj, 'method') wraps the method and returns a mock.
The original implementation still runs.
Call spy.mockRestore() after the test to undo the spy.
solution:
const blacksmith={hammer(item){return`forged: ${item}`;}};
test('spy tracks calls',()=>{const spy=jest.spyOn(blacksmith,'hammer');const result=blacksmith.hammer('sword');expect(result).toBe('forged: sword');expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith('sword');spy.mockRestore();});

title: Spy with mockReturnValue
story: Override the oracle's answer with a spy while still being able to restore it later.
objective: Use jest.spyOn + mockReturnValue to override a method's return value.
hints: jest.spyOn(obj, method).mockReturnValue(val) — spy + override return.
mockRestore() undoes the spy and restores the original implementation.
Without mockRestore, the override persists across tests.
solution:
const oracle={predict(){return Math.random()>0.5?'victory':'defeat';}};
test('oracle predicts victory',()=>{const spy=jest.spyOn(oracle,'predict').mockReturnValue('victory');expect(oracle.predict()).toBe('victory');spy.mockRestore();});

title: Spy on Math.random
story: Control fate itself — spy on Math.random to make dice deterministic.
objective: Use jest.spyOn to mock Math.random.
hints: jest.spyOn(Math, 'random') wraps the global Math.random.
mockReturnValue(0.5) makes it always return 0.5.
Always restore after the test.
solution:
function rollDice(){return Math.floor(Math.random()*6)+1;}
test('dice rolls 4',()=>{const spy=jest.spyOn(Math,'random').mockReturnValue(0.5);expect(rollDice()).toBe(4);spy.mockRestore();});

title: mockClear vs mockReset
story: After each skirmish, clear the battle records. Know the difference between clearing and resetting.
objective: Demonstrate the difference between mockClear (clears calls) and mockReset (clears calls + implementation).
hints: mockClear() — zeroes call count and instances, keeps implementation.
mockReset() — does everything mockClear does, plus removes implementation.
mockRestore() — restores original implementation (spyOn only).

title: beforeAll and afterAll
story: The expedition takes time to prepare and debrief. Use beforeAll/afterAll for one-time setup.
objective: Use beforeAll to set up once before all tests and afterAll to clean up.
hints: beforeAll runs once before all tests in the scope.
afterAll runs once after all tests in the scope.
Use for expensive setup like DB connections (unlike beforeEach).

title: Nested describe Scoping
story: The palace has outer halls and inner chambers. Each scope has its own setup.
objective: Use nested describe blocks to scope beforeEach differently per group.
hints: Inner beforeEach runs AFTER outer beforeEach.
Outer beforeEach sets 'outer hall', then inner sets 'inner chamber'.
Test outside describe uses only the outer beforeEach.

title: test.skip
story: The broken bridge must be skipped for now. Mark tests to skip without deleting them.
objective: Use test.skip to skip a test and keep it in the file.
hints: test.skip() or xtest() — marks the test as skipped (shown in output).
The skipped test will not run but appears in the report.
Use .only to run only specific tests during debugging.

`expect(value).toMatchObject(partial)` checks that an object **contains** the expected subset — extra properties are ignored.

```
const user = { id: 1, name: 'Aria', role: 'Mage', level: 99 };
expect(user).toMatchObject({ name: 'Aria', role: 'Mage' }); // passes
```

`toMatchSnapshot()` captures the value on first run and compares on subsequent runs.

title: test.todo
story: The treasure map shows unexplored zones. Mark them with todo for future expeditions.
objective: Use test.todo to mark tests that need to be written.
hints: test.todo('description') — appears in output as a reminder.
No callback allowed — only the description string.
Useful for planning tests alongside implementation.

title: jest.useFakeTimers()
story: The time mage can freeze the clock. Replace real timers with fakes to test setTimeout.
objective: Use jest.useFakeTimers() and jest.runAllTimers() to test setTimeout.
hints: jest.useFakeTimers() replaces setTimeout, setInterval etc. with fakes.
jest.runAllTimers() fires all pending timers immediately.
Always call before the test code that uses timers.

title: advanceTimersByTime
story: The hourglass advances precisely. Use advanceTimersByTime to control exactly when callbacks fire.
objective: Use jest.advanceTimersByTime(ms) to advance the clock by a specific amount.
hints: jest.advanceTimersByTime(ms) moves the fake clock forward by ms milliseconds.
Only timers scheduled within that window will fire.
Call it multiple times to simulate time passing in steps.

title: setInterval with Fake Timers
story: The siege cannon fires every 500ms. Test the interval fires repeatedly.
objective: Use jest.useFakeTimers and advance time to test setInterval.
hints: setInterval fires every N ms — advancing 1500ms with 500ms interval = 3 fires.
jest.advanceTimersByTime fires all timers that fall within that window.
Check both call count and arguments.

title: runOnlyPendingTimers
story: Only fire the timers already scheduled — not new ones they trigger.
objective: Use jest.runOnlyPendingTimers() to fire only currently pending timers.
hints: runOnlyPendingTimers() fires currently queued timers but not new ones they schedule.
Call it again to fire the next batch.
Compare to runAllTimers which fires everything recursively.
explanation:
`expect(array).toContain(item)` checks that an array includes a value (using `===`).
`expect(array).toContainEqual(obj)` does deep equality for objects in arrays.

```
expect([1, 2, 3]).toContain(2);
expect([{ name: 'Aria' }]).toContainEqual({ name: 'Aria' });
expect('Hello World').toContain('World'); // works on strings too
```

title: test.each — Array of Arrays
story: The alchemist needs to verify the same formula with many ingredients. Use test.each.
objective: Use test.each with an array of arrays for parameterized tests.
hints: test.each([[a,b,result], ...]) runs a test for each row.
%i in the name is replaced with the integer argument.
Parameters are passed in order to the test callback.
solution:
function add(a,b){return a+b;}
test.each([[1,2,3],[0,0,0],[-1,1,0],[100,200,300]])('add(%i,%i) equals %i',(a,b,expected)=>{expect(add(a,b)).toBe(expected);});
explanation:

```
expect([1, 2, 3]).toContain(2);
expect([{ name: 'Aria' }]).toContainEqual({ name: 'Aria' });
expect('Hello World').toContain('World'); // works on strings too
```

title: test.each — Object Array
story: The merchant catalogue uses named fields. Use test.each with object rows.
objective: Use test.each with an array of objects for named test parameters.
hints: Object rows allow named parameters — use destructuring in callback.
$fieldName in the test name string is replaced with the value.
Much more readable than positional arrays for complex inputs.
solution:
function discount(p,pct){return p*(1-pct/100);}
test.each([{price:100,pct:10,expected:90},{price:200,pct:50,expected:100},{price:50,pct:0,expected:50}])('$price at $pct% discount is $expected',({price,pct,expected})=>{expect(discount(price,pct)).toBe(expected);});
explanation:

expect([{ name: 'Aria' }]).toContainEqual({ name: 'Aria' });
expect('Hello World').toContain('World'); // works on strings too
```

title: describe.each
story: Multiple character classes need the same test suite. Use describe.each for full group parameterization.
objective: Use describe.each to run an entire describe block with different data.
hints: describe.each([...])(...) runs the full describe block for each row.
%s formats a string argument in the describe name.
Each row gets its own describe block with all its tests.
solution:
function getAttack(cls){const a={warrior:50,mage:80,rogue:60};return a[cls]||0;}
describe.each([['warrior',50],['mage',80],['rogue',60]])('%s class',(cls,exp)=>{test(`${cls} correct attack`,()=>{expect(getAttack(cls)).toBe(exp);});test(`${cls} attack positive`,()=>{expect(getAttack(cls)).toBeGreaterThan(0);});});
explanation:

expect([{ name: 'Aria' }]).toContainEqual({ name: 'Aria' });
expect('Hello World').toContain('World'); // works on strings too
```

title: Edge Cases with test.each
story: Test the boundaries of the dungeon walls — 0, negative, max values.
objective: Use test.each to cover boundary/edge cases for a function.
hints: test.each is perfect for boundary testing.
Boundaries (min, max) and out-of-range values are classic edge cases.
Document expected values clearly in the test name format string.
solution:
function clamp(v,min,max){return Math.min(Math.max(v,min),max);}
test.each([[5,0,10,5],[-5,0,10,0],[15,0,10,10],[0,0,10,0],[10,0,10,10]])('clamp(%i,%i,%i)=%i',(v,min,max,exp)=>{expect(clamp(v,min,max)).toBe(exp);});
explanation:
`expect(array).toContain(item)` checks that an array includes a value (using `===`).
`expect(array).toContainEqual(obj)` does deep equality for objects in arrays.

```
expect([1, 2, 3]).toContain(2);
expect([{ name: 'Aria' }]).toContainEqual({ name: 'Aria' });
expect('Hello World').toContain('World'); // works on strings too
```

title: Testing Class Methods
story: The Knight class must prove it can attack and defend correctly.
objective: Write tests for a class with multiple methods.
hints: Use beforeEach to create a fresh instance for each test.
Test each method independently.
Test both happy path and edge cases (hp = 0).
solution:
class Knight{constructor(n,hp){this.name=n;this.hp=hp;}attack(){return 50;}defend(d){this.hp-=d;return this.hp;}isAlive(){return this.hp>0;}}
describe('Knight',()=>{let k;beforeEach(()=>{k=new Knight('Arthur',100);});test('attack',()=>{expect(k.attack()).toBe(50);});test('defend',()=>{expect(k.defend(30)).toBe(70);});test('isAlive',()=>{expect(k.isAlive()).toBe(true);});test('dead',()=>{k.hp=0;expect(k.isAlive()).toBe(false);});});

title: Spy on Class Method
story: Monitor the wizard's cast method without interrupting the spell.
objective: Use jest.spyOn to spy on a class instance method.
hints: jest.spyOn works on class instances, not just plain objects.
The real method still executes.
spy.mockRestore() removes the spy after the test.
solution:
class Wizard{cast(s){return`casting: ${s}`;}}
test('spy on cast',()=>{const w=new Wizard();const spy=jest.spyOn(w,'cast');w.cast('fireball');w.cast('ice bolt');expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith('fireball');spy.mockRestore();});

title: mockImplementationOnce
story: The shape-shifter only transforms once, then reverts to normal form.
objective: Use mockImplementationOnce to return different results for the first call only.
hints: Chain .mockImplementationOnce(fn) before .mockImplementation(fn).
Once-values are consumed first, then the default kicks in.
You can chain multiple mockImplementationOnce for a sequence.

title: expect.objectContaining()
story: The hero's stats object has many fields. Only assert on the ones you care about.
objective: Use expect.objectContaining() to do partial object matching inside assertions.
hints: expect.objectContaining({...}) — passes if the object contains those keys with those values.
Extra keys in the received object are ignored.
Useful when objects have dynamic fields like timestamps.
solution:
function createHero(name){return{name,hp:100,mp:50,level:1,createdAt:new Date().toISOString()};}
test('hero has name and level',()=>{const h=createHero('Aragorn');expect(h).toEqual(expect.objectContaining({name:'Aragorn',level:1}));});

title: expect.stringContaining()
story: The battle log must mention the hero's name — you don't care about the exact message.
objective: Use expect.stringContaining() to do partial string matching.
hints: expect.stringContaining(str) — passes if the string includes str.
Works inside toEqual, toMatchObject etc.
Use expect.stringMatching(regex) for pattern matching.

title: toStrictEqual
story: The shapeshifter appears identical but its true type betrays it. Use toStrictEqual.
objective: Understand the difference between toEqual and toStrictEqual.
hints: toStrictEqual checks object types (class matters).
toStrictEqual distinguishes sparse arrays from arrays with undefined.
Use toEqual for general deep equality, toStrictEqual when class identity matters.

title: Testing Error Types
story: Different cursed artifacts throw different error types. Assert the exact error type.
objective: Use toThrow with a specific Error class and message.
hints: toThrow(TypeError) — checks instanceof TypeError.
toThrow(/pattern/) — checks message with regex.
Always wrap the call in () => to let Jest catch the throw.

title: Async Error with async/await
story: The vault API rejects bad keys asynchronously. Catch the async error.
objective: Use try/catch in an async test to handle rejected promises.
hints: Option 1: await expect(openVault('bad')).rejects.toThrow('invalid key')
Option 2: try { await openVault('bad') } catch(e) { expect(e.message).toContain('invalid key') }
Always pair with expect.assertions(1) when using try/catch.

title: Sharing State Safely
story: The guild register must be fresh for each test. Shared state between tests causes flaky failures.
objective: Use beforeEach to ensure each test starts with a clean state.
hints: Without beforeEach, tests share the same register instance.
State from one test pollutes the next (test order matters — bad).
Always use beforeEach to reset shared state.

title: Multiple Spies
story: Spy on both the king's messenger and his treasurer simultaneously.
objective: Use multiple jest.spyOn calls in one test and assert on both.
hints: Create multiple spies independently for different methods.
Restore each spy after the test to avoid cross-test pollution.
Order of assertions does not matter.
solution:
const court={sendMessage(m){return`sent: ${m}`;},transferGold(a){return`transferred: ${a}`;}};
test('king issues orders',()=>{const ms=jest.spyOn(court,'sendMessage');const gs=jest.spyOn(court,'transferGold');court.sendMessage('prepare for war');court.transferGold(1000);expect(ms).toHaveBeenCalledWith('prepare for war');expect(gs).toHaveBeenCalledWith(1000);ms.mockRestore();gs.mockRestore();});

title: Boss: The Mock Gauntlet
story: Face the Mock Gauntlet — combine jest.fn(), mockReturnValueOnce, spyOn, and assertion matchers in one epic test.
objective: Combine multiple mocking techniques in a single test suite.
hints: Use mockReturnValueOnce for first call, mockReturnValue for fallback.
jest.spyOn preserves the original — check return value AND call.
Restore spies after each test.

title: Boss: Async + Mocks
story: The final dungeon combines async fetching with mocked dependencies. Conquer both.
objective: Write an async test that uses a mocked async dependency.
hints: mockResolvedValue on a spy makes it return a resolved promise.
await the function under test.
The spy intercepts the DB call — getItemName gets the mocked data.

title: Your First Snapshot
story: The wizard wants to freeze time and compare past vs present. Snapshot testing saves the day.
objective: Use toMatchSnapshot() to capture and compare output.
hints: toMatchSnapshot() saves output on first run and compares on subsequent runs.
If snapshot changes intentionally, run jest --updateSnapshot.
Works with strings, objects, arrays.
solution:
function greet(n){return`Hello, ${n}!`;}
test('greet snapshot',()=>{expect(greet('World')).toMatchSnapshot();});

title: Object Snapshot
story: The artifact details must be preserved exactly. Snapshot the whole object.
objective: Snapshot a plain object to detect unexpected changes.
hints: toMatchSnapshot() deep-serialises objects.
Any key added or changed will fail the test.
Update with --updateSnapshot when changes are intentional.
solution:
function getArtifact(){return{id:1,name:'Sword of Truth',damage:50};}
test('artifact snapshot',()=>{expect(getArtifact()).toMatchSnapshot();});

title: Inline Snapshot
story: The scribe wants the expected value written right in the scroll. Use inline snapshots.
objective: Use toMatchInlineSnapshot() with the expected string inline.
hints: toMatchInlineSnapshot(`"OK"`) — value goes directly in the test file.
Jest auto-fills the argument on first run if you leave it empty.
Backtick template literal wraps the expected serialised string.
solution:
function status(c){return c===200?'OK':'Error';}
test('status inline snapshot',()=>{expect(status(200)).toMatchInlineSnapshot(`"OK"`);});

title: not.toBe
story: Two heroes must be different people. Assert they are NOT the same reference.
objective: Use .not.toBe() to assert two objects are not the same reference.
hints: .not inverts any matcher.
.toBe uses Object.is (reference equality).
{} !== {} even if contents match — that's what not.toBe checks.
solution:
const h1={name:'Alice'},h2={name:'Alice'};
test('different references',()=>{expect(h1).not.toBe(h2);});

title: not.toEqual
story: Two spells must have different effects. Deep-compare and assert they differ.
objective: Use .not.toEqual() to assert two objects have different values.
hints: .not.toEqual does deep inequality check.
.toEqual and .not.toEqual are mirrors.
{damage:10} and {damage:20} are not deeply equal.
solution:
const s1={damage:10},s2={damage:20};
test('spells differ',()=>{expect(s1).not.toEqual(s2);});

title: not.toContain
story: The banned item must not appear in the hero's inventory.
objective: Use .not.toContain() to assert an array does not include a value.
hints: .not.toContain checks item is absent from array.
Also works on strings: expect(str).not.toContain(substr).
Uses strict equality for array item checks.
solution:
const inv=['sword','shield','potion'];
test('no cursed item',()=>{expect(inv).not.toContain('cursed ring');});

title: not.toBeNull and not.toBeUndefined
story: The quest result must actually exist — it must be neither null nor undefined.
objective: Use .not.toBeNull() and .not.toBeUndefined() together.
hints: .not.toBeNull() — value is not null.
.not.toBeUndefined() — value is not undefined.
toBeDefined() is the short form for not.toBeUndefined.
solution:
function findQuest(id){return id===1?{name:'Slay the Dragon'}:null;}
test('quest exists',()=>{const r=findQuest(1);expect(r).not.toBeNull();expect(r).not.toBeUndefined();});

title: toBeDefined
story: The merchant must have a price set before selling. Verify the price is defined.
objective: Use toBeDefined() to verify a value is not undefined.
hints: toBeDefined() — not undefined.
toBeUndefined() — is undefined.
These are opposites of each other.

title: toHaveBeenCalledTimes
story: The blacksmith must be called exactly twice — once to forge, once to temper.
objective: Use toHaveBeenCalledTimes(n) to verify exact call count.
hints: toHaveBeenCalledTimes(n) — mock was called exactly n times.
Works only on jest.fn() or jest.spyOn targets.
Use toHaveBeenCalled() if you only care it was called at least once.
solution: test('forge called twice',()=>{const forge=jest.fn();forge('sword');forge('shield');expect(forge).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);});

Multiple calls chain in order.

Chain multiple calls for sequential async values.
