title: Clearing Mock State
story: Between battles, the hero resets. Clear a mock's recorded state without removing its implementation.
objective: Use mockClear() to reset call history but keep return value.
hints: mockClear() resets calls, instances, results — NOT implementation.
mockReset() also removes implementation/return values.
mockRestore() restores original (only for spyOn).
solution: test('mock clear',()=>{const a=jest.fn().mockReturnValue('hit');a();a();expect(a).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);a.mockClear();expect(a).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(0);expect(a()).toBe('hit');});

title: Resetting Mocks
story: The weapon must be fully reset — no memory, no power. Use mockReset.
objective: Use mockReset() to clear state AND remove implementation.
hints: mockReset() clears everything including return values.
After reset, mock returns undefined by default.
Use in afterEach to ensure clean state per test.
solution: test('mock reset',()=>{const p=jest.fn().mockReturnValue(100);p();p.mockReset();expect(p).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(0);expect(p()).toBeUndefined();});

title: toThrowError with Message
story: The vault throws a specific error when the wrong key is used. Verify the message.
objective: Use toThrow() with a string to match the error message.
hints: toThrow(string) checks the error message contains that string.
toThrow(ErrorClass) checks the instance type.
toThrow(/regex/) matches with a regular expression.
solution:
function openVault(k){if(k!=='secret')throw new Error('Invalid key');return'open';}
test('wrong key throws message',()=>{expect(()=>openVault('wrong')).toThrow('Invalid key');});

title: toThrow with Regex
story: The incantation error message follows a pattern. Match it with a regular expression.
objective: Use toThrow(/regex/) to pattern-match error messages.
hints: toThrow(/pattern/) tests message against regex.
The regex only needs to match a substring.
Use ^ and $ anchors for exact matches.
solution:
function cast(s){if(!s)throw new Error('Spell cannot be empty');return'casting';}
test('empty spell error',()=>{expect(()=>cast('')).toThrow(/cannot be empty/);});

title: Custom Error Classes
story: The dungeon uses typed errors — a DungeonError, not a generic Error.
objective: Throw and test a custom error class with toThrow(ClassName).
hints: toThrow(ClassName) checks instanceof.
You can combine: toThrow(DungeonError) plus a message check.
Custom errors extend Error and set this.name.

title: toHaveLength on String
story: The hero's name must be exactly 5 characters. Check string length.
objective: Use toHaveLength() on a string.
hints: toHaveLength(n) works on strings and arrays.
It checks .length property.
Use not.toHaveLength for inequality.
solution:
const h='Arwen';
test('name length',()=>{expect(h).toHaveLength(5);});

title: toHaveLength on Array
story: The party must have exactly 3 members. Check the array length.
objective: Use toHaveLength() on an array.
hints: toHaveLength(n) reads .length on any value.
Works with strings, arrays, objects with .length.
Prefer over expect(arr.length).toBe(n).
solution:
const p=['Alice','Bob','Carol'];
test('party size',()=>{expect(p).toHaveLength(3);});

title: toContainEqual
story: The treasure chest contains an item. But we only know its shape, not its reference.
objective: Use toContainEqual() to find an object by value in an array.
hints: toContainEqual uses deep equality (like toEqual).
toContain uses reference equality — different for objects.
Useful when you recreate the expected object in the test.
solution:
const chest=[{id:1,name:'Gold Coin'},{id:2,name:'Ruby'}];
test('ruby is in chest',()=>{expect(chest).toContainEqual({id:2,name:'Ruby'});});

title: expect.not.arrayContaining
story: None of the banned items should be in the approved list.
objective: Use expect.not.arrayContaining() inside toEqual.
hints: expect.not.arrayContaining(arr) — none of arr's items are in the received array.
Used as an argument inside another matcher like toEqual.
Useful for exclusion assertions.
solution:
const a=['sword','shield','potion'];
test('no banned items',()=>{expect(a).toEqual(expect.not.arrayContaining(['bomb','poison']));});

title: Return a Rejected Promise
story: The forbidden spell always fails. Return the rejected promise and catch with .rejects.
objective: Return a rejected promise and assert with .rejects.toThrow().
hints: Return the assertion so Jest waits for it.
rejects.toThrow() unwraps the rejection and checks the error.
Alternatively use async/await with try/catch.
solution:
function forbiddenSpell(){return Promise.reject(new Error('Forbidden'));}
test('spell is forbidden',()=>{return expect(forbiddenSpell()).rejects.toThrow('Forbidden');});

title: Async Error with try/catch
story: The async dungeon hatch throws if blocked. Use try/catch to verify.
objective: Use async/await with try/catch to assert async errors.
hints: async/await lets you use try/catch naturally.
The catch block can contain expect calls.
Add expect.assertions(1) to ensure the catch block ran.
solution:
async function openHatch(l){if(l)throw new Error('Hatch is locked');return'open';}
test('locked hatch throws',async()=>{try{await openHatch(true);}catch(e){expect(e.message).toBe('Hatch is locked');}});

title: expect.assertions with async
story: The test must prove it ran all the checks — use expect.assertions to enforce it.
objective: Use expect.assertions(n) to ensure async assertions execute.
hints: expect.assertions(1) ensures exactly one assertion is called.
If the catch block never runs, the test fails due to 0 assertions.
Great guard for async error paths.
solution:
async function fetchData(){return Promise.reject(new Error('network error'));}
test('async assertions run',async()=>{expect.assertions(1);try{await fetchData();}catch(e){expect(e.message).toBe('network error');}});

title: Spy on Object Method
story: Track when the healer uses their ability, without changing their real power.
objective: Use jest.spyOn to spy on an object method while keeping the real implementation.
hints: jest.spyOn wraps the real method — it still runs unless you stub it.
Always call mockRestore() to clean up after a spy.
Use mockImplementation to override the real function.
solution:
const healer={heal(a){return`Healed ${a} HP`;}};
test('heal was called',()=>{const spy=jest.spyOn(healer,'heal');healer.heal(50);expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(50);expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);spy.mockRestore();});

title: Spy and Override Return
story: The oracle's real answer is hidden. Override it with a controlled response.
objective: Use jest.spyOn with mockReturnValue to override a method's return.
hints: Chain .mockReturnValue() directly on spyOn for immediate stubbing.
spy.mockRestore() restores the original implementation.
Without mockRestore, the stub persists between tests.
solution:
const oracle={predict(){return Math.random()>0.5?'victory':'defeat';}};
test('controlled prophecy',()=>{const spy=jest.spyOn(oracle,'predict').mockReturnValue('victory');expect(oracle.predict()).toBe('victory');expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalled();spy.mockRestore();});

title: test.only
story: Focus the investigation on one suspect. Only run one test in the suite.
objective: Use test.only() to run a single test and skip the rest.
hints: test.only (or fit) runs only that test in the file.
All other tests are skipped automatically.
Use describe.only to focus an entire describe block.
explanation:
Custom matchers from `jest-dom` (`@testing-library/jest-dom`) extend `expect` with DOM-specific assertions:

```
expect(element).toBeInTheDocument();    // exists in DOM
expect(element).toBeVisible();          // not hidden
expect(element).toBeDisabled();         // has disabled attr
expect(element).toHaveClass('active');  // has CSS class
expect(element).toHaveValue('text');    // input value
expect(element).toHaveFocus();          // currently focused
```

title: describe.only
story: Focus the entire investigation block on the vault section.
objective: Use describe.only() to focus on one describe block.
hints: describe.only runs only that block — all other describes are skipped.
test.only and describe.only follow the same pattern.
Also available as fdescribe (in some environments).
solution:
describe.only('vault tests',()=>{test('vault opens',()=>{expect('open').toBe('open');});});
describe('skipped tests',()=>{test('never runs',()=>{expect(false).toBe(true);});});

objective: Use nested describe() blocks to organise related tests.
hints: Nest describe() calls to group related tests.
Each describe can have its own beforeEach/afterEach.
Test names show full path: Dungeon > Entrance > door opens.

title: test.concurrent
story: Multiple scouts report simultaneously. Run async tests concurrently.
objective: Use test.concurrent() to run async tests in parallel.
hints: test.concurrent runs tests at the same time (async only).
Useful for I/O-heavy tests that don't share state.
Avoid shared mutable state with concurrent tests.
solution:
test.concurrent('scout 1',async()=>{const r=await Promise.resolve('north clear');expect(r).toBe('north clear');});
test.concurrent('scout 2',async()=>{const r=await Promise.resolve('south clear');expect(r).toBe('south clear');});

title: jest.runAllTimers
story: Fast-forward through all pending timeouts at once to resolve them instantly.
objective: Use jest.runAllTimers() to flush all pending timers.
hints: jest.runAllTimers() flushes all pending timers synchronously.
Unlike advanceTimersByTime, it resolves all regardless of delay.
Careful: recursive timers can cause infinite loops.
solution:
jest.useFakeTimers();
test('run all timers',()=>{let count=0;setTimeout(()=>{count++;},100);setTimeout(()=>{count++;},500);setTimeout(()=>{count++;},1000);jest.runAllTimers();expect(count).toBe(3);});

title: jest.runAllTicks
story: Microtasks queue up before the next event loop tick. Flush them all at once.
objective: Use jest.runAllTicks() to flush the microtask queue (process.nextTick).
hints: jest.runAllTicks() flushes the nextTick queue.
Different from runAllTimers which handles setTimeout/setInterval.
Useful when code uses process.nextTick for deferred work.
solution:
jest.useFakeTimers();
test('flush microtasks',()=>{let done=false;process.nextTick(()=>{done=true;});jest.runAllTicks();expect(done).toBe(true);});

title: jest.setSystemTime
story: The dungeon clock must be frozen at midnight for the ritual.
objective: Use jest.setSystemTime() to control Date.now() and new Date().
hints: jest.setSystemTime(date) fixes the clock at that moment.
new Date() and Date.now() both use the frozen time.
Must call jest.useFakeTimers() first.
solution:
jest.useFakeTimers();
test('frozen clock',()=>{const m=new Date('2024-01-01T00:00:00Z');jest.setSystemTime(m);expect(new Date().toISOString()).toBe('2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z');expect(Date.now()).toBe(m.getTime());});

title: test.each with Tagged Template
story: The spell tome lists names and damages in a readable table. Use tagged template test.each.
objective: Use test.each with tagged template literal syntax.
hints: Tagged template syntax: test.each`col1 | col2\n ${val1} | ${val2}`.
Column names become object keys in the test function.
$column in the test name is replaced with the value.

title: describe.each Advanced
story: Each hero class has a set of tests. Run the same describe block for all classes.
objective: Use describe.each to parameterise an entire describe block.
hints: describe.each creates one describe block per row.
%s formats the name in the describe label.
Each row's values are passed as arguments to the callback.
solution: describe.each([['Warrior',100,'sword'],['Mage',60,'staff']])('%s hero',(name,hp,weapon)=>{test('has positive HP',()=>{expect(hp).toBeGreaterThan(0);});test('has a weapon',()=>{expect(weapon).toBeTruthy();});});

title: Boss: The Parameterised Gauntlet
story: A hundred challenges survived. Now combine test.each, matchers, and async in one battle.
objective: Write parameterised async tests combining numeric and string matchers.
hints: Async test.each functions just add async before the callback.
%i formats integers, %s formats strings in test names.
Combine multiple expects per test for thorough coverage.
solution:
async function fetchHero(id){const h=[{id:1,name:'Alice',hp:100},{id:2,name:'Bob',hp:80}];return h.find(x=>x.id===id)||null;}
test.each([[1,'Alice',100],[2,'Bob',80]])('hero %i: %s with %i HP',async(id,name,hp)=>{const h=await fetchHero(id);expect(h).not.toBeNull();expect(h.name).toBe(name);expect(h.hp).toBe(hp);expect(h.hp).toBeGreaterThan(0);});

title: Branch Coverage
story: Every path through the enchanted gate must be tested — true and false branches.
objective: Write tests for both branches of an if/else.
hints: Branch coverage means testing every if/else path.
Write one test per distinct return path.
This achieves 100% branch coverage for classify().

Each test should have a clear input → expected output.
Group pure util tests with describe for organisation.

objective: Test that a function mutates an object and assert with toEqual.

Since fillPotion mutates in place, the original object changes.
Test the state of the object after the call.

function fillPotion(b,l){b.contents=l;b.full=true;return b;}
test('bottle is filled',()=>{const b={contents:null,full:false};fillPotion(b,'mana');expect(b).toEqual({contents:'mana',full:true});});

objective: Test a function returning an array using toEqual and toHaveLength.
hints: toHaveLength checks the .length property.
Access individual elements with index notation.
Combine multiple expects for thorough verification.
solution:
function getQuests(d){const a=[{id:1,name:'Slay Rats',difficulty:'easy'},{id:2,name:'Kill Boss',difficulty:'hard'},{id:3,name:'Gather Herbs',difficulty:'easy'}];return a.filter(q=>q.difficulty===d);}

title: Testing a Class Constructor
story: The Adventurer is born with a name and starting HP. Test its initial state.
objective: Test a class constructor by creating an instance and asserting its properties.
hints: Instantiate the class with new inside the test.
Assert each property individually with toBe or toEqual.
Use toBeInstanceOf(Adventurer) to check the type.
solution:
class Adventurer{constructor(n){this.name=n;this.hp=100;this.level=1;}}
test('adventurer initial state',()=>{const h=new Adventurer('Aria');expect(h.name).toBe('Aria');expect(h.hp).toBe(100);expect(h.level).toBe(1);});

title: Testing Class Methods
story: The Adventurer can take damage. Test that takeDamage reduces HP correctly.
objective: Test a class method that mutates instance state.
hints: Create a fresh instance for each test to avoid state leakage.
Math.max ensures HP never goes negative.
Test boundary conditions: exact damage, overkill.

title: Testing Getters
story: The hero's status is derived from HP. Test the computed getter.
objective: Test a JavaScript getter property on a class.
hints: Access getter like a property: hero.status, not hero.status().
Create fresh instances with different HP values.
Test all branches: > 50, 1-50, 0.

title: Testing Static Methods
story: The Adventurer factory creates heroes from raw data. Test the static factory method.
objective: Test a static method that creates an instance from data.
hints: Call static methods on the class: Adventurer.fromData().
Test default parameter handling by omitting the field.
toBeInstanceOf(Adventurer) can verify the returned type.

title: Boss: Class Integration
story: The Adventurer class is complete. Constructor, methods, getters — test it all.
objective: Write a comprehensive test suite for a multi-method class.
hints: Test each method in isolation with a fresh instance.
Getters are tested like properties.
Boundary: 250 XP → Math.floor(250/100)+1 = 3.

title: Testing Callbacks with done
story: The messenger delivers asynchronously. Use the done callback to signal completion.
objective: Use the done callback to test async callback-based code.
hints: Jest waits for done() before ending the test.
If done is never called, Jest times out.
Call done(error) to fail the test with an error message.
solution:
function deliverMessage(cb){setTimeout(()=>cb('message delivered'),10);}
test('delivery confirmed',(done)=>{deliverMessage((r)=>{expect(r).toBe('message delivered');done();});});

title: Callback Error Handling
story: The courier may fail. Pass the error to done() to signal failure correctly.
objective: Pass errors to done() when a callback receives an error.
hints: done(err) fails the test with the given error.
Pattern: if (err) return done(err); then assertions.
This mirrors the Node.js error-first callback convention.
solution:
function riskyDelivery(s,cb){setTimeout(()=>{if(s)cb(null,'delivered');else cb(new Error('Failed'),null);},10);}
test('successful delivery',(done)=>{riskyDelivery(true,(err,r)=>{if(err)return done(err);expect(r).toBe('delivered');done();});});

title: toMatchObject Partial
story: The quest report has many fields. Only verify the critical ones with toMatchObject.
objective: Use toMatchObject() to partially match an object.
hints: toMatchObject only checks the specified keys.
Extra keys in the received object are ignored.
Useful when you only care about a subset of properties.
solution:
const r={id:42,status:'complete',reward:500,completedAt:'2024-01-15',hero:'Alice'};
test('report has key fields',()=>{expect(r).toMatchObject({status:'complete',reward:500});});

title: expect.objectContaining Nested
story: The hero's nested stats only need partial verification. Use objectContaining inside an array.
objective: Use expect.objectContaining inside toEqual for array elements.
hints: expect.objectContaining works inside arrays.
It ignores extra keys on each element.
Combine with expect.arrayContaining for any-order matching.
solution:
const team=[{name:'Alice',stats:{hp:100,mp:50}},{name:'Bob',stats:{hp:80,mp:70}}];
test('team members partial match',()=>{expect(team).toEqual([expect.objectContaining({name:'Alice'}),expect.objectContaining({name:'Bob'})]);});

title: toBeNaN
story: Dividing by zero yields NaN. The calculator must identify this dangerous result.
objective: Use toBeNaN() to assert a value is NaN.
hints: toBeNaN() checks Number.isNaN(value).
0/0 in JavaScript is NaN.
Note: 1/0 is Infinity, not NaN.

title: toBeFinite — check with not
story: Division by zero also produces Infinity. Verify that valid results are finite.
objective: Use not.toBeNaN() and explicit checks for finite values.
hints: Combine not.toBeNull() and not.toBeNaN() to verify a valid numeric result.
toBe(5) handles the exact value check.
Guard clauses return null instead of NaN/Infinity.

title: Mock a Dependency Inline
story: The shop depends on a price service. Replace it with a mock for isolated testing.
objective: Replace a dependency on an object with a jest.fn mock.
hints: Dependency injection makes mocking easy — pass the mock in the constructor.
jest.fn().mockReturnValue() creates a stub.
Verify both the return value AND that the mock was called correctly.

title: Mock Multiple Methods
story: The dungeon API has multiple endpoints. Mock all of them for a unit test.
objective: Mock an object with multiple jest.fn methods and verify each.
hints: Mock objects can have multiple jest.fn properties.
Each mock records its own calls independently.
toEqual does deep comparison for returned objects.
solution:
function QuestManager(api){this.start=(id)=>api.startQuest(id);this.complete=(id)=>api.completeQuest(id);}
test('quest lifecycle',()=>{const api={startQuest:jest.fn().mockReturnValue({started:true}),completeQuest:jest.fn().mockReturnValue({reward:100})};const qm=new QuestManager(api);const s=qm.start(1);const c=qm.complete(1);expect(s).toEqual({started:true});expect(c).toEqual({reward:100});expect(api.startQuest).toHaveBeenCalledWith(1);expect(api.completeQuest).toHaveBeenCalledWith(1);});

title: Async Mock with Implementation
story: The dungeon database is async. Mock it with a custom async implementation.
objective: Use mockImplementation with an async function.
hints: mockImplementation takes a function (sync or async) as the mock body.
For async mocks, the function can be async or return a Promise.
mockResolvedValue is shorthand for async returning a value.

title: Boss: Full Mock Suite
story: A century of tests completed. The mock master challenge awaits.
objective: Combine spies, mock implementations, call assertions, and async in one suite.
hints: mockResolvedValue for happy path, null for not-found path.
rejects.toThrow checks both rejection and message.
Verify all side effects: db called, logger called.

title: Testing reduce
story: The treasurer tallies gold from multiple chests. Test the reduction.
objective: Test a function that uses .reduce() to sum values.
hints: reduce with initial value 0 handles empty arrays.
toEqual for objects, toBe for primitives.
Test the empty case to cover the edge.

title: Testing find and findIndex
story: The archivist searches scrolls by title. Test find and findIndex.
objective: Test functions using .find() and .findIndex().
hints: find returns the element or undefined.
findIndex returns -1 when not found.
toEqual for the found object, toBe for the index.

title: Testing every and some
story: The guild checks if all heroes are ready, or if any hero is injured.
objective: Test functions using .every() and .some().
hints: every returns true only if ALL elements pass the predicate.
some returns true if AT LEAST ONE element passes.
Test both true and false cases for full coverage.

title: Testing flat and flatMap
story: Dungeon rooms contain nested loot arrays. Flatten them for the inventory.
objective: Test functions using .flat() and .flatMap().
hints: flat() flattens one level deep by default.
flatMap() maps then flattens (one level).
toEqual for array comparisons.

title: Testing Object.keys and values
story: The wizard inspects the spell registry. Test Object.keys() and Object.values().
objective: Test functions using Object.keys() and Object.values().
hints: Object.keys returns an array of string keys.
Object.values returns an array of values.
Spread into Math.max for the maximum value.

title: String Manipulation Tests
story: The scribe transforms hero names. Test trim, split, and join.
objective: Test string methods: trim, split, join.
hints: trim() removes leading/trailing whitespace.
split(' ') splits on spaces.
join('.') joins array elements with dots.

title: Regex Matching Tests
story: The guard checks if hero IDs follow the pattern HERO-XXXX.
objective: Test a function that validates a string with a regex.
hints: Use toBe(true/false) for boolean regex test results.
Test valid, invalid prefix, and invalid length.
^ and $ anchor the regex to the full string.

title: Template Literal Tests
story: The herald formats proclamations with template literals. Test the output.
objective: Test a function that builds strings with template literals.
hints: toBe checks exact string equality.
toMatch checks substring containment.

title: LRU Cache
story: The dungeon caches only the most recent 3 rooms. Test LRU eviction.
objective: Test an LRU cache implementation with get and set.
hints: Map preserves insertion order — oldest is first.
get() moves the accessed key to the end (most recent).
set() evicts the first (least recently used) key when full.
solution:
class LRUCache{constructor(c){this._cap=c;this._cache=new Map();}get(k){if(!this._cache.has(k))return -1;const v=this._cache.get(k);this._cache.delete(k);this._cache.set(k,v);return v;}set(k,v){if(this._cache.has(k))this._cache.delete(k);else if(this._cache.size>=this._cap){this._cache.delete(this._cache.keys().next().value);}this._cache.set(k,v);}}
test('lru eviction',()=>{const lru=new LRUCache(2);lru.set(1,'a');lru.set(2,'b');lru.get(1);lru.set(3,'c');expect(lru.get(2)).toBe(-1);expect(lru.get(1)).toBe('a');expect(lru.get(3)).toBe('c');});

title: Boss: Algorithms Gauntlet
story: 210 levels complete. The algorithms gauntlet — data structures, memoization, and mocks.
objective: Combine LRU cache, binary search, and mock logging in one suite.
hints: First search(5) is a miss — binary search runs.
Second search(5) is a hit — returns cached result.
Verify both logger.miss and logger.hit call counts.
solution:
class SearchCache{constructor(c,l){this._lru=new Map();this._cap=c;this._log=l;}search(a,t){if(this._lru.has(t)){this._log.hit(t);return this._lru.get(t);}let lo=0,hi=a.length-1,result=-1;while(lo<=hi){const mid=Math.floor((lo+hi)/2);if(a[mid]===t){result=mid;break;}if(a[mid]<t)lo=mid+1;else hi=mid-1;}this._log.miss(t);if(this._lru.size>=this._cap)this._lru.delete(this._lru.keys().next().value);this._lru.set(t,result);return result;}}
test('cache miss then hit',()=>{const logger={hit:jest.fn(),miss:jest.fn()};const sc=new SearchCache(2,logger);const arr=[1,3,5,7,9];const r1=sc.search(arr,5);const r2=sc.search(arr,5);expect(r1).toBe(2);expect(r2).toBe(2);expect(logger.miss).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);expect(logger.hit).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);});

title: Circuit Breaker Pattern
story: The dungeon circuit breaker opens after 3 failures, blocking further calls.
objective: Test a circuit breaker that opens after threshold failures.
hints: After 3 failures, circuit opens and blocks further calls.
The 4th call throws 'Circuit open' without calling fail.
fail should only be called 3 times total.
solution:
function makeCircuitBreaker(t){let failures=0,open=false;return async function call(fn){if(open)throw new Error('Circuit open');try{const r=await fn();failures=0;return r;}catch(e){failures++;if(failures>=t)open=true;throw e;}};}
test('opens after threshold failures',async()=>{const cb=makeCircuitBreaker(3);const fail=jest.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error('fail'));for(let i=0;i<3;i++){await expect(cb(fail)).rejects.toThrow('fail');}await expect(cb(fail)).rejects.toThrow('Circuit open');expect(fail).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);});

title: Middleware Chain
story: The dungeon request passes through a chain of middlewares. Test the pipeline.
objective: Test a compose-style middleware chain.
hints: Middlewares execute like a stack: in order forward, reverse on the way back.

solution:
function compose(...mws){return function(ctx,next){let index=-1;function dispatch(i){if(i<=index)throw new Error('next() called multiple times');index=i;const fn=mws[i]||next;if(!fn)return;fn(ctx,()=>dispatch(i+1));}dispatch(0);}}
test('middleware chain executes in order',()=>{const log=[];const mw1=(ctx,next)=>{log.push('mw1 in');next();log.push('mw1 out');};const mw2=(ctx,next)=>{log.push('mw2 in');next();log.push('mw2 out');};const handler=compose(mw1,mw2);handler({},(()=>log.push('final')));expect(log).toEqual(['mw1 in','mw2 in','final','mw2 out','mw1 out']);});

title: Pub/Sub with History
story: The dungeon event bus replays missed events to new subscribers.

hints: Replaying sends past events to the new subscriber.

solution:
class HistoryBus{constructor(){this._subs={};this._history={};}publish(e,d){this._history[e]=this._history[e]||[];this._history[e].push(d);(this._subs[e]||[]).forEach(fn=>fn(d));}subscribe(e,fn,replay=false){this._subs[e]=this._subs[e]||[];this._subs[e].push(fn);if(replay)(this._history[e]||[]).forEach(fn);}}
test('replay on subscribe',()=>{const bus=new HistoryBus();bus.publish('hero',{name:'Alice'});bus.publish('hero',{name:'Bob'});const handler=jest.fn();bus.subscribe('hero',handler,true);expect(handler).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);expect(handler).toHaveBeenCalledWith({name:'Alice'});});

  setTimeout(() => results.push(3), 300)
  await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300)

objective: Create a context with http_credentials={'username': 'user', 'password': 'pass'}. Navigate to level-01 (which doesn't need auth). Print 'LEVEL_PASSED'.
starterCode:
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch()
    context = browser.new_context(
        http_credentials={'username': 'user', 'password': 'pass'}
    )
    page = context.new_page()
    page.goto('http://localhost:5000/pages/level-01/')

    # TODO: print 'LEVEL_PASSED'

    context.close()
    browser.close()
hints: http_credentials sets Basic Auth credentials for the context.
Level-01 doesn't require auth, so it navigates fine.
Just print 'LEVEL_PASSED'.

```python
context = browser.new_context(http_credentials={'username': 'user', 'password': 'pass'})
print('LEVEL_PASSED')
```
solution:
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

    browser = p.chromium.launch()
    context = browser.new_context(http_credentials={'username': 'user', 'password': 'pass'})
    page = context.new_page()
    page.goto('http://localhost:5000/pages/level-01/')
    print('LEVEL_PASSED')
